data.title: Quantum Computers Are Poised to Crack Encryption. AI Could Beat Them to It. — WSJ
data.description:
By Christopher Mims

What if the mathematical locks and keys that secure our bank accounts, email inboxes and everything else on the internet turn out to be a lot less secure than we thought? What if the password-protected internet we rely on every day collapses?

Quantum computers have long threatened such an apocalypse. For decades, engineers have been preparing for their arrival — and their inevitable abuse by well-heeled bad guys.

The result is known as "postquantum cryptography." According to leading mathematics experts, an orderly transition of the world's digital systems to this new paradigm should avert an event that could otherwise send us back a century, technology-wise.

But now there is a potentially more pressing issue: AI's impressive math skills.

Artificial intelligence is pushing advances in various mathematics fields at an unprecedented rate, conquering problems that our puny human minds have wrestled with for centuries. The fear is that this could include new solutions to the math problems that keep our encrypted communications encrypted.

Math all the way down

For encryption to continue to work, our assumptions about the algorithms that make it possible must remain true. One such assumption is that some mathematical operations are easy to solve in one direction, yet hard to reverse. The classic example: Multiplying two large prime numbers is simple enough, while factoring the very lengthy result back into those two prime numbers is essentially impossible with conventional computers.

But some cryptographers argue that we might not be able to count on this remaining the case.

"A lot of what makes us feel like cryptography is secure is because a lot of smart people have looked at crypto for a long time, and we didn't find anything," says Matthew Green, a cryptographer and associate professor at Johns Hopkins University, on mathematicians' ongoing search for code-breaking formulas. "But what we're learning is that human beings looking at things is not the gold standard — it's not relevant anymore."

It's reminiscent of the cryptographic race during World War II. Alan Turing and his team at Bletchley Park, innovating on an electromechanical system pioneered by Polish engineers, found a way to crack Germany's infamous Enigma code. Many great minds thought Enigma was unbeatable, but Turing's device proved them wrong.

Green cites recent breakthroughs in mathematics by AI labs, including a partial solution to the infamously challenging Navier Stokes equations, and a more recent breakthrough disproving the Exponential Time Hypothesis.

It's this second result that has some researchers especially worried. This long-held hypothesis suggests that certain problems don't have shortcuts. The only way to solve them is to take the long way. But if the hypothesis is false, it could render decades of research in theoretical computer science irrelevant. If there are shortcuts to solving these problems, then those shortcuts could make it far easier to crack "uncrackable" encryption.

Vitalik Buterin is the creator of the Ethereum protocol which underpins much of modern cryptocurrency systems. In early October, before the latest breakthrough math results from OpenAI and Anthropic, he issued a warning on X: "We should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography."

On Monday, he reiterated the warning at the Ethereum Foundation's annual conference in Mumbai, calling for "post-AI cryptography."

Green cautions that there's no evidence the world's cryptographic algorithms have already been cracked, but he thinks the next AI-powered math breakthroughs could touch more directly on cryptography's foundational math.

The white whale of cryptography

How worried should we be? That's the subject of fierce debate among experts.

Baseless speculation about an impending collapse of the world's online security isn't just premature, it can be irresponsible, argues Yehuda Lindell, head of cryptography at Coinbase and a computer-science professor currently on leave from Israel's Bar-Ilan University.

"Anything is possible," says Lindell. "But speculating that bad things can happen is something which just doesn't help anyone."

Lindell objects in particular to claims that postquantum cryptographic algorithms, which are gradually being implemented, might be vulnerable enough to AI's mathematical discoveries to force us to rethink the safeguards. He says evidence points to the opposite: These algorithms are likely to withstand most attacks by any kind of computer. Also, he says it is possible AI will help us strengthen our cryptographic algorithms.

At worst, he adds, engineers might have to lengthen cryptographic keys, the numbers used in secure exchanges. This would slow down the encoding and decoding that constantly occurs in our online interactions, but it wouldn't make things unusable.

The reason cryptography experts find themselves at odds is because of a disagreement about fundamental mathematical questions that remain unresolved.

Those like Green, who are concerned over cryptographic algorithms collapsing under AI innovation, worry that somewhere out there in the world of mathematics is an as-yet-undiscovered white whale. If a discovery is made that makes even some "impossible" math problems solvable with today's computers, our digital locks could weaken.

Experts on Lindell's side believe decades of work by mathematicians suggest such a possibility is vanishingly small. "My claim isn't that AI will not help with cryptographic analysis — I think it very likely will," he says. Yet he believes the fundamental mathematical assumption that holds up his entire field — that there really are hard problems that will never be solved by a shortcut — will stand the test of time.

Even in the worst-case scenario, Lindell would rather an AI lab like OpenAI or Anthropic make the discovery that modern cryptography is insecure, since these companies have a history of disclosing vulnerabilities so that engineers can patch them.

"We don't want a system to be broken by North Korea, and then they don't tell anybody else," he adds.

Green, on the other hand, is worried that since cryptographic systems take years to update, discreet disclosures won't be enough. "I definitely think that we don't have any idea what's coming," he says.

Write to Christopher Mims at christopher.mims@wsj.com

data.title: Havertys Furniture Fourth Quarter 2026 Cash Dividend
data.description:
ATLANTA, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Haverty Furniture Companies, Inc. ( and HVT.A)  ("Havertys" or the "Company") today announced that its Board of Directors declared a cash dividend to be paid on the outstanding shares of the two classes of $1 par value common stock of the Company at a rate of $0.33 per share on the common stock and $0.31 per share on the Class A common stock. The dividend is payable on December 9, 2026, to stockholders of record at the close of business on November 23, 2026. Havertys Furniture has paid a cash dividend each year since 1935.

About Havertys Furniture

Haverty Furniture Companies, Inc. ( and HVT.A), established in 1885, is a full-service home furnishings retailer with 131 showrooms in 18 states in the Southern and Midwestern regions, providing its customers with a wide selection of quality merchandise in middle to upper-middle price ranges. Additional information is available on the Company's website at www.havertys.com.

SOURCE Haverty Furniture Companies, Inc.

data.title: AMTD IDEA, AMTD Digital and TGE Jointly Announce the Injection of Four Premium Hotel Assets into TGE
data.description:
PARIS and NEW YORK and LONDON, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AMTD IDEA Group (; ), a NYSE and SGX-ST dual-listed company and a subsidiary of AMTD Group Inc. ("AMTD Group"), AMTD Digital Inc. ("AMTD Digital") (), a controlled and consolidated subsidiary of AMTD IDEA Group, and The Generation Essentials Group ("TGE") (; ), a controlled and consolidated subsidiary of AMTD Digital, jointly announced today the injection of four premium hotel assets into TGE.

On October 21, 2026, AMTD Digital and TGE entered into an Asset Transfer and Share Issuance Agreement (the "Asset Transfer Agreement"), pursuant to which AMTD Digital transferred, on November 2, 2026 to TGE its controlling interests in four hotel assets, consisting of 100% of the AMTD IDEA Tribeca Hotel, a 50% equity interest with veto power in the hotel operations of the Ritz-Carlton, Perth, and 100% of AMTD Dao By Dorsett Hornsey London, and 80% of Upper Regalia Kuala Lumpur (collectively, the "Target Assets"), for an aggregate purchase price of US$209,766,000, factoring into consideration also the underlying debts.

The L'Officiel Coffee and Bar celebrated its official opening at City of Dreams in Macao SAR in September 2026. As the Brand's second global location, it reinforces our commitment to a strategic expansion plan within the hospitality sector, with a target of establishing 15 to 20 additional venues worldwide.

The purchase price was satisfied in full by the issuance by TGE to AMTD Digital on November 2, 2026 of 198,630,381 newly issued Class A ordinary shares of TGE (the "Consideration Shares"), determined based on the 30-day volume-weighted average price of TGE's shares on the New York Stock Exchange for the thirty trading days ending on May 29, 2026. The Asset Transfer Agreement was entered into immediately after AMTD IDEA Group transferred the Target Assets into AMTD Digital at the valuation and through settlement and discharge of US$209,766,000 of indebtedness owed by AMTD IDEA Group to AMTD Digital (collectively, the "Transactions").

The Transactions are intended to inject and consolidate the group's premium hospitality assets under TGE, which focuses on hospitality and VIP services, among other businesses focusing into lifestyle and experiencing.

After the consummation of the Transactions and as of the date of this press release, (i) AMTD Digital holds 88.2% of the issued and outstanding share capital of TGE, representing 91.1% of the total outstanding voting power of TGE, and (ii) AMTD IDEA Group, directly and through AMTD Digital, beneficially owns 95.6% of the issued and outstanding share capital of TGE, representing 96.7% of the total outstanding voting power of TGE.

About AMTD Group

AMTD Group is a conglomerate with a core business portfolio spanning across media and entertainment, education and training, and premium assets and hospitality sectors.

About AMTD IDEA Group

AMTD IDEA Group (; ) represents a diversified institution and digital solutions conglomerate group, connecting companies and investors with global markets. Its comprehensive one-stop business services plus digital solutions platform addresses different clients' diverse and inter-connected business needs and digital requirements across all phases of their life cycles. AMTD IDEA Group is uniquely positioned as an active super connector between clients, business partners, investee companies, and investors, connecting the East and the West. For more information, please visit www.amtdinc.com or follow us on X (formerly known as "Twitter") at @AMTDGroup.

About AMTD Digital Inc.

AMTD Digital Inc. () is a comprehensive digital solutions platform headquartered in France. Its one-stop digital solutions platform operates key business lines including digital media, content and marketing services, investments as well as hospitality and VIP services. For AMTD Digital's announcements, please visit https://ir.amtdigital.net/investor-news.

About The Generation Essentials Group

The Generation Essentials Group (; ), jointly established by AMTD Group, AMTD IDEA Group (; ) and AMTD Digital Inc. (), is headquartered in France and focuses on global strategies and developments in multi-media, entertainment, and cultural affairs worldwide as well as hospitality and VIP services. TGE comprises L'Officiel, The Art Newspaper, movie and entertainment projects. Collectively, TGE is a diversified portfolio of media and entertainment businesses, and a global portfolio of premium properties. Also, TGE is a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) sponsor manager, with its first SPAC successfully raised and priced on December 18, 2025.
